name: Lazy Peons
summary: Foreman Thazz'ril sends new Horde recruits across the Valley of Trials to rouse sleeping peons. Their labor keeps timber moving to Durotar's settlements.

sections.title: Slacking in the Sun
sections.body: Durotar's new homes need timber, stone, and hard labor. Peons have little skill in battle, so they carry much of that burden and keep the Horde supplied with workers. In the Valley of Trials, heat and grueling work drive Foreman Thazz'ril's crews beneath the trees for unauthorized naps.

sections.title: A Swift Wake-Up Call
sections.body: Foreman Thazz'ril gives new Horde recruits his blackjack and sends them across the valley to wake the sleeping workers. Startled, the peons return to chopping wood. Their labor keeps lumber flowing for Durotar's survival.

faq.q: Why are the peons falling asleep?
faq.answer: Hauling heavy lumber beneath Durotar's punishing sun is exhausting work. When no supervisor is near, peons slip beneath large trees to rest.
Foreman Thazz'ril oversees the labor crews in the Valley of Trials. They harvest lumber and supplies for the Horde's new construction.
The Foreman's Blackjack is a heavy leather sap Thazz'ril uses to discipline workers who shirk their duties. A blow to the head wakes a sleeping peon without causing permanent injury.

faq.q: What role do peons have in the Horde?
faq.answer: Peons make up the laboring class of orcish society. Though physically stout, they are considered unfit for war and instead build, mine, and cut wood for Horde settlements and its war machine.

faq.q: Where do I find the sleeping peons?
faq.answer: You can find sleeping peons throughout the Valley of Trials, both north and south of the Den. Look beneath wide tree canopies where workers seek shade.

faq.q: What happens after the peons are awakened?
faq.answer: After you return the blackjack to Foreman Thazz'ril, he sends you to recover his lost mining pick from a nearby cave.

angles.text: As a young orc coming of age, you learn the hard truths and practical discipline of building a nation from the wilderness by disciplining your kin's workers.
As a Darkspear troll training alongside your allies, you see the brute strength and exasperation behind orcish construction.
As a member of the Horde, you know every Durotar outpost depends on timber harvested by peons. Keeping the workers on the job matters to all.
